newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi gives tourism venture new deadline to pay up.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi gives tourism venture new deadline to pay up.

text.p: Vietnam has given Maryland-based BBI Investment Group until the end of this month to come up with an initial deposit of $2 million for a joint-venture tourism project near coastal Danang city, media reports said on Tuesday.
The Ministry of Planning and Investment had threatened to withdraw the licence for the $243 million beach resort because BBI had not deposited the funds into the venture's bank account.

"To facilitate the development of the project, the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI) has allowed the foreign partner to extend the deadline for transferring $2 million to the JV company's account...until 30 November, 1996," the Thanh Nien newspaper said.
A ministry official declined to comment on the reports in Thanh Nien and the MPI-controlled Dau Tu (Investment) magazine.
BBI President Robert Bernstein told reporters in Hanoi last May that talks with the MPI had succeeded in paving over differences threatening the project.

Describing the matter as a misunderstanding and oversight, he said that instead of making a deposit at the joint venture's bank, BBI had spent more than the required $2 million on costs directly associated with the project.
He said at the time that BBI, a closely held investment group, had deposited $100,000 in the joint venture account and had agreed with the MPI to provide the remainder within 90 days.

The Dau Tu magazine said BBI must pay the deposit, secure a loan for the whole project and submit a new plan for its implementation by the new deadline or face the possibility of a licence withdrawal.
However, it said that if BBI could only secure part of the loan, it could submit plans for a downsized project to the authorities for approval.
